components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 推 is to push.
隹 (zhuī) is a loose hint for tuī; 堆 duī and 谁 shéi share it.
钅 (metal, from 金) — marks metals, as in 钱, 铁, 银; 销 first meant melting metal, then to sell off.
肖 (xiāo) gives the sound exactly: 销 xiāo, also in 消 xiāo and 宵 xiāo.

example.hanzi: 这个销售员擅长推销产品。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoshòuyuán shàncháng tuīxiāo chǎnpǐn.
example.english: This salesperson is skilled at marketing products.
example.fact: The door-to-door vacuum cleaner salesman became a cultural icon in the early 20th century United States. Companies like Fuller Brush and later Electrolux built entire national sales forces around direct home demonstrations, a marketing model that dominated appliance sales until television advertising took over after the 1950s.

examples.hanzi: 他在街上向路人推销保险。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiē shàng xiàng lùrén tuīxiāo bǎoxiǎn.
examples.english: He's selling insurance to passersby on the street.

examples.hanzi: 这个新产品很难推销出去。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xīn chǎnpǐn hěn nán tuīxiāo chūqù.
examples.english: This new product is hard to sell.

components.note: 尸 (body, a crouching figure) — also in 屁 and 屎; 尿 is body plus 水 (water).
水 (water) — liquid passed from the body.
巾 (cloth) — 巾 is a cloth radical, as in 帽 hat, 带 belt; 布 is cloth, and by extension to spread or announce, as in 宣布.

example.hanzi: 妈妈正在给宝宝换尿布。
example.pinyin: Māma zhèngzài gěi bǎobao huàn niàobù.
example.english: Mom is changing the baby's diaper.
example.fact: Disposable diapers were invented in the early 1950s by Swedish engineer and mother Marion Donovan, though major manufacturers initially rejected her design. Victor Mills, a Procter & Gamble chemist, later refined the concept into what became Pampers, launched commercially in 1961.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝的尿布湿了,该换了。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao de niàobù shī le, gāi huàn le.
examples.english: The baby's diaper is wet and needs changing.

examples.hanzi: 我去超市买了一包新尿布。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù chāoshì mǎile yì bāo xīn niàobù.
examples.english: I went to the supermarket and bought a pack of new diapers.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 巾 is a cloth radical, as in 帽 hat, 带 belt; 布 is cloth, and by extension to spread or announce, as in 宣布.
艹 (grass, plants) — plant radical for herbs and greens, as in 花, 草, 菜; 莱 originally named a weed.
来 (lái) — same sound as 莱 — handy since 莱 mostly appears in foreign names like 好莱坞.
心 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 想, 爱, 思; 恩 is kindness, gratitude of the heart.
因 (yīn) is only a loose sound hint for ēn.

example.hanzi: 我的朋友叫布莱恩,他来自加拿大。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou jiào Bùláiēn, tā láizì Jiānádà.
example.english: My friend is called Brian; he is from Canada.
example.fact: Canada has the world's longest coastline of any country, stretching approximately 202,080 kilometers, about 125,570 miles. That is longer than the coastlines of the next several countries on the list combined.

examples.hanzi: 布莱恩和我是大学同学。
examples.pinyin: Bùláiēn hé wǒ shì dàxué tóngxué.
examples.english: Brian and I were college classmates.

examples.hanzi: 布莱恩明天要来我们家吃晚饭。
examples.pinyin: Bùláiēn míngtiān yào lái wǒmen jiā chī wǎnfàn.
examples.english: Brian is coming to our house for dinner tomorrow.

components.note: 今 (now, today) — gives sound to 琴 qín, 含 hán, 念 niàn and 吟 yín; the old picture is uncertain.
日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.

example.hanzi: 今日新闻头条是关于气候变化的报道。
example.pinyin: Jīnrì xīnwén tóutiáo shì guānyú qìhòu biànhuà de bàodào.
example.english: Today's headline news is a report about climate change.
example.fact: The Keeling Curve, a continuous record of atmospheric carbon dioxide levels measured atop Hawaii's Mauna Loa volcano since 1958, is one of science's longest-running direct climate datasets. It shows CO2 levels rising in nearly every year measured, apart from brief pandemic-related dips.

examples.hanzi: 今日天气晴朗,适合出游。
examples.pinyin: Jīnrì tiānqì qínglǎng, shìhé chūyóu.
examples.english: Today is sunny and good for an outing.

examples.hanzi: 本店今日休息,明天再来吧。
examples.pinyin: Běn diàn jīnrì xiūxi, míngtiān zài lái ba.
examples.english: This shop is closed today; come back tomorrow.

components.note: 宀 (roof, house) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家 home, 室 room, 安 safe; 宣 was a large hall, where proclamations are made.
言 (speech) — the traditional form of 讠: words and speech; an oath is a spoken promise.
折 (zhé, to break) — a promise you must not break; zhé is only a loose sound hint for shì.

example.hanzi: 新总统在就职典礼上宣誓。
example.pinyin: Xīn zǒngtǒng zài jiùzhí diǎnlǐ shàng xuānshì.
example.english: The new president swore an oath at the inauguration ceremony.
example.fact: George Washington's 1789 presidential oath is traditionally said to have ended with the words 'so help me God,' though the phrase does not appear in the oath specified by the U.S. Constitution. Most historians consider the phrase's origin, while widely repeated by later presidents, historically unverifiable.

examples.hanzi: 战士们在国旗下宣誓。
examples.pinyin: Zhànshìmen zài guóqí xià xuānshì.
examples.english: The soldiers took an oath under the national flag.

examples.hanzi: 证人在法庭上宣誓说真话。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngrén zài fǎtíng shàng xuānshì shuō zhēnhuà.
examples.english: The witness swore in court to tell the truth.

components.note: 足 (foot) — marks feet and walking, as in 跑 run, 跳 jump, 路 road; 蹦 is bouncing or jumping.
崩 (bēng) — close sound: 蹦 bèng. 崩 also sounds out 绷 bēng.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在草地上又蹦又跳。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài cǎodì shang yòu bèng yòu tiào.
example.english: The kids are bouncing and jumping about on the grass.
example.fact: 蹦 describes springy hopping with both feet: 蹦蹦跳跳 (skipping about) and 蹦极 (bungee jumping, phonetic-plus-sense). 蹦迪 is slang for going clubbing.

examples.hanzi: 小兔子在草地上蹦来蹦去。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo tùzi zài cǎodì shàng bèng lái bèng qù.
examples.english: The little rabbit is hopping around on the grass.

examples.hanzi: 他高兴得蹦了起来。
examples.pinyin: Tā gāoxìng de bèng le qǐlái.
examples.english: He was so happy that he jumped up.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 肚 is the belly.
土 (tǔ) — near sound — 肚 is dù; 土 also sounds out 吐 tǔ.

example.hanzi: 我肚子饿了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ dùzi è le.
example.english: I'm hungry.
example.fact: Standing alone, 肚 normally means the belly, read dù, and 肚子 is the colloquial word for stomach or belly (我肚子疼 'my stomach hurts'). Read dǔ it means tripe, as in 爆肚, a Beijing dish.

examples.hanzi: 我吃了太多，肚子有点疼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chī le tài duō, dùzi yǒudiǎn téng.
examples.english: I ate too much and my stomach hurts a bit.

examples.hanzi: 他喝了一肚子水。
examples.pinyin: Tā hē le yí dùzi shuǐ.
examples.english: He drank a bellyful of water.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water and rivers, as in 河, 海; 源 is the spring where water starts.
原 (yuán) gives the sound exactly: 源 yuán, also in 愿 yuàn.

example.hanzi: 这条河的源头在山里。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé de yuántóu zài shān lǐ.
example.english: The source of this river is in the mountains.
example.fact: 源 appears in 资源 (resources), 来源 (source), 电源 (power supply), 源头 (headwaters) and 开源 (open source). It is also a surname.

examples.hanzi: 这条河的水源很干净。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé de shuǐyuán hěn gānjìng.
examples.english: The water source of this river is very clean.

examples.hanzi: 他在找问题的根源。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhǎo wèntí de gēnyuán.
examples.english: He is looking for the root of the problem.

components.note: 要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.

example.hanzi: 快点走,要不我们会迟到的。
example.pinyin: Kuài diǎn zǒu, yàobù wǒmen huì chídào de.
example.english: Hurry up, or else we'll be late.
example.fact: Mechanical clocks with a verge-and-foliot escapement first appeared in European monasteries around the 13th century. They were built primarily to ring bells calling monks to prayer at precise canonical hours, and only became widespread for everyday timekeeping centuries later.

examples.hanzi: 要不我们明天再去吧?今天太累了。
examples.pinyin: Yàobù wǒmen míngtiān zài qù ba? Jīntiān tài lèi le.
examples.english: How about we go tomorrow? We're too tired today.

examples.hanzi: 你要不先吃点东西,要不去睡一会儿。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yàobù xiān chī diǎn dōngxi, yàobù qù shuì yíhuìr.
examples.english: Either eat something first, or go sleep for a while.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
田 here replaces 囟 (skull) in the older form: head over heart
心 (heart) — thinking and feeling, as in 想, 意, 感: 思 is to think over, with head and heart.

example.hanzi: 我猜不透她的心思。
example.pinyin: Wǒ cāi bú tòu tā de xīnsi.
example.english: I can't figure out what's on her mind.
example.fact: Studies in cognitive psychology have repeatedly shown that humans are poor at accurately judging others' emotions from facial expressions alone, with average accuracy only slightly better than chance in many controlled experiments. Popular claims about reliably reading 'micro-expressions' are far less consistent than television crime dramas suggest.

examples.hanzi: 他最近总是心思不在工作上。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn zǒngshì xīnsi bú zài gōngzuò shàng.
examples.english: Lately his mind is never on his work.

examples.hanzi: 她花了很多心思准备这份礼物。
examples.pinyin: Tā huāle hěn duō xīnsi zhǔnbèi zhè fèn lǐwù.
examples.english: She put a lot of thought into preparing this gift.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and trade, as in 财, 货, 贵; 贩 is to trade goods.
反 (fǎn) hints at the sound: 贩 fàn is close to 饭 fàn.
龶 (plant-like top) — dictionary reads the top as 'a poisonous plant'. Memory aid: a plant growing on top of a mother (母) is something you must not eat.
母 (mǔ, mother) — the bottom part and radical. Sound clue is lost today (毒 is dú); use it as a visual memory aid, as in 母亲.

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了一名贩毒嫌疑人。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dàibǔle yī míng fàndú xiányírén.
example.english: Police arrested a drug trafficking suspect.
example.fact: The 19th-century Opium Wars between Britain and Qing-dynasty China were triggered in large part by the British East India Company's massive opium trafficking into China. The Qing government tried and failed to suppress the trade, ultimately ceding Hong Kong to Britain after its defeat.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的主角是一个贩毒集团的老大。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de zhǔjué shì yí gè fàndú jítuán de lǎodà.
examples.english: The protagonist of the film is the boss of a drug-trafficking ring.

examples.hanzi: 贩毒是严重的犯罪行为。
examples.pinyin: Fàndú shì yánzhòng de fànzuì xíngwéi.
examples.english: Drug trafficking is a serious crime.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.
刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".

example.hanzi: 他们在机场依依不舍地道别。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài jīchǎng yīyī-bùshě de dàobié.
example.english: They said a reluctant goodbye at the airport.
example.fact: Heathrow Airport's Terminal 5 in London has one of the busiest arrivals halls in the world. Researchers studying it in the mid-2000s found that reunion embraces there typically lasted around three seconds on average, a small quantifiable pattern from behavioral studies of nonverbal greeting rituals.

examples.hanzi: 我挥挥手,跟朋友们道别。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huīhuī shǒu, gēn péngyoumen dàobié.
examples.english: I waved and said goodbye to my friends.

examples.hanzi: 他没来得及跟老师道别就走了。
examples.pinyin: Tā méi láidejí gēn lǎoshī dàobié jiù zǒu le.
examples.english: He left without having time to say goodbye to the teacher.

components.note: 木 (wood) — a wooden cabinet; also in 桌 table, 椅 chair.
巨 (jù) is only a stand-in; the traditional 櫃 used 贵 guì for the sound.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 衣服都放在柜子里。
example.pinyin: Yīfu dōu fàng zài guìzi lǐ.
example.english: The clothes are all kept in the cabinet.
example.fact: Traditional Chinese Ming-dynasty furniture makers, especially those working with huanghuali rosewood, often built cabinets using elaborate mortise-and-tenon joinery with no metal nails or glue at all. The joints were cut so precisely that the wood could expand and contract with humidity without the piece falling apart.

examples.hanzi: 我把杯子放进了厨房的柜子里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ bēizi fàngjìnle chúfáng de guìzi lǐ.
examples.english: I put the cups in the kitchen cupboard.

examples.hanzi: 这个柜子太高了,我够不着。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guìzi tài gāo le, wǒ gòu bù zháo.
examples.english: This cabinet is too tall for me to reach.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water and washing, as in 洗 wash, 游 swim, 洗澡; 浴 is a bath.
谷 (yù/gǔ) gives the sound: 浴 yù, also in 欲 yù and 裕 yù.

example.hanzi: 他在浴室里唱歌。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yùshì lǐ chànggē.
example.english: He is singing in the bathroom.
example.fact: 浴 is a formal, written word for bathing: 浴室 (bathroom), 浴缸 (bathtub), 淋浴 (shower), 沐浴 (to bathe). In ordinary speech 洗澡 is the usual verb, while 浴 sits in nouns and signage.

examples.hanzi: 我每天晚上都要洗浴。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān wǎnshang dōu yào xǐyù.
examples.english: I take a bath every evening.

examples.hanzi: 酒店的浴室很干净。
examples.pinyin: Jiǔdiàn de yùshì hěn gānjìng.
examples.english: The hotel bathroom is very clean.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 勃 is vigorous, as in 蓬勃 flourishing and 勃然 suddenly.
孛 (bèi) — close sound: 勃 bó. 孛 also sounds out 脖 bó.

example.hanzi: 这座城市生机勃勃。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì shēngjī bóbó.
example.english: This city is full of vitality.
example.fact: 勃 is often doubled or placed in set phrases: 生机勃勃 (full of vitality), 野心勃勃 (full of ambition), 兴致勃勃 (in high spirits) and 勃然大怒 (flaring up in anger).

examples.hanzi: 春天到了，草地上生机勃勃。
examples.pinyin: Chūntiān dào le, cǎodì shàng shēngjī bóbó.
examples.english: Spring has come, and the meadow is full of life.

examples.hanzi: 他听了这话，勃然大怒。
examples.pinyin: Tā tīng le zhè huà, bórán dà nù.
examples.english: Hearing this, he flew into a rage.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord words: 红 red, 给 give, 线 line; a thread has an end, which fits 终 end.
冬 (dōng) rhymes with 终 zhōng, and 冬 originally meant the end (of the year) too — so it helps sound and sense.
身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.

example.hanzi: 他获得了终身教授的职位。
example.pinyin: Tā huòdéle zhōngshēn jiàoshòu de zhíwèi.
example.english: He obtained the position of tenured (lifelong) professor.
example.fact: The concept of academic tenure in the United States was formalized in the 1940 Statement of Principles on Academic Freedom and Tenure, jointly issued by the American Association of University Professors and the Association of American Colleges. It was largely a response to earlier incidents of professors being fired for expressing unpopular political views.

examples.hanzi: 这是我终身难忘的一课。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ zhōngshēn nánwàng de yí kè.
examples.english: This is a lesson I'll never forget in my life.

examples.hanzi: 结婚是人生的终身大事。
examples.pinyin: Jiéhūn shì rénshēng de zhōngshēn dàshì.
examples.english: Marriage is a lifelong major event.

components.note: 史 (history) — a hand 又 holding a record, the scribe. 史 sounds the same as 使 shǐ and 驶 shǐ.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: hidden indoors, secret.
宓 (mì) gives the exact sound; also in 蜜 mì.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.hanzi: 史密斯先生是这家公司的首席执行官。
example.pinyin: Shǐmìsī xiānsheng shì zhè jiā gōngsī de shǒuxí zhíxíngguān.
example.english: Mr. Smith is the CEO of this company.
example.fact: Smith is the most common surname in both the United States and the United Kingdom, originating as an occupational name for a metalworker, someone who 'smites' or hammers metal. Related surnames like Schmidt in German and Kovač in Slavic languages carry the same meaning in their own languages.

examples.hanzi: 史密斯夫妇下周要搬到北京。
examples.pinyin: Shǐmìsī fūfù xiàzhōu yào bāndào Běijīng.
examples.english: Mr. and Mrs. Smith are moving to Beijing next week.

examples.hanzi: 我的英语老师姓史密斯,是个很风趣的人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de Yīngyǔ lǎoshī xìng Shǐmìsī, shì gè hěn fēngqù de rén.
examples.english: My English teacher is named Smith and is a very witty person.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.
寸 (hand, inch) — a hand, as in 对, 寻, 守; with 圭 (a heap of earth) it means heaping earth to mark a border, then to seal.

example.hanzi: 她把信纸装进信封里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ xìnzhǐ zhuāngjìn xìnfēng lǐ.
example.english: She put the letter paper into the envelope.
example.fact: The first adhesive postage stamp, Britain's Penny Black, was introduced in 1840 alongside a standardized flat postal rate. Mass-produced pre-gummed envelopes followed soon after, made possible by an envelope-folding machine patented in 1845 that could fold roughly 2,700 envelopes an hour.

examples.hanzi: 请把信封上的地址写清楚。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ xìnfēng shàng de dìzhǐ xiě qīngchu.
examples.english: Please write the address on the envelope clearly.

examples.hanzi: 他在红色的信封里放了一些钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài hóngsè de xìnfēng lǐ fàngle yìxiē qián.
examples.english: He put some money in a red envelope.

components.note: 几 (small table) — a low table with legs. As a sound it gives jī to 机 and 肌, and means how many in 几个.
千 (thousand) — 千 is a number built on the old form of 人 with an extra stroke; its sound is also in 迁 qiān.

example.hanzi: 这个体育场可以容纳几千名观众。
example.pinyin: Zhège tǐyùchǎng kěyǐ róngnà jǐqiān míng guānzhòng.
example.english: This stadium can hold several thousand spectators.
example.fact: Rome's Colosseum, completed in 80 AD, could seat an estimated 50,000 to 80,000 spectators. It featured a network of underground passages and elevators, called the hypogeum, used to hoist animals and gladiators directly up into the arena floor.

examples.hanzi: 他手里有几千块钱,想去旅行。
examples.pinyin: Tā shǒu lǐ yǒu jǐqiān kuài qián, xiǎng qù lǚxíng.
examples.english: He has a few thousand yuan and wants to travel.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市里有几千家小餐馆。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì lǐ yǒu jǐ qiān jiā xiǎo cānguǎn.
examples.english: There are thousands of small restaurants in this city.

components.note: 广 (building, shelter) — the roof-and-wall frame, as in 店, 床, 度. Here it is mostly the outline of the old 應.
心 (heart) — hidden in the traditional 應, 'respond from the heart'; simplification dropped it. 应 is yīng (should) or yìng (respond).
當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).

example.hanzi: 我们应当遵守交通规则。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yīngdāng zūnshǒu jiāotōng guīzé.
example.english: We should obey traffic rules.
example.fact: The world's first traffic light was installed in London in 1868, a gas-lit semaphore signal designed to control horse-drawn carriage traffic near the Houses of Parliament. It exploded after only a few months of use, injuring its police operator, and modern electric traffic signals did not become common until decades later in the United States.

examples.hanzi: 大家应当互相帮助。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā yīngdāng hùxiāng bāngzhù.
examples.english: We should all help each other.

examples.hanzi: 你应当早点告诉他真相。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yīngdāng zǎodiǎn gàosu tā zhēnxiàng.
examples.english: You ought to have told him the truth earlier.

components.note: 长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".
勹 (wrap) — the visible part, a bent shape. Memory aid: a stooped figure under weight, wearing down over time — a long time, as in 好久.
灸 (jiǔ, moxibustion) — 久 is its sound part, same sound jiǔ. Another is 玖 jiǔ. The old picture of 久 is disputed.

example.hanzi: 他们保持着长久的友谊。
example.pinyin: Tāmen bǎochízhe chángjiǔ de yǒuyì.
example.english: They have maintained a long-lasting friendship.
example.fact: A pair of Greenland sharks, among the longest-lived vertebrates known, are estimated by radiocarbon dating of their eye lenses to live 250 to 500 years. Some individuals swimming in the North Atlantic today may have been alive since the 16th century.

examples.hanzi: 这样做不是长久之计。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò bú shì chángjiǔ zhī jì.
examples.english: Doing it this way is not a long-term solution.

examples.hanzi: 我希望我们的合作能长久。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng wǒmen de hézuò néng chángjiǔ.
examples.english: I hope our cooperation can last.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 拍 is clapping or patting with the hand, also used for filming and taking photos.
白 (bái) — loose hint — 拍 is pāi; 白 also sounds out 伯 bó and 怕 pà.

example.hanzi: 这部电影将于下个月正式开拍。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiāng yú xià ge yuè zhèngshì kāipāi.
example.english: This film will officially begin shooting next month.
example.fact: The 1977 film 'Star Wars' had such a troubled and expensive production that 20th Century Fox executives reportedly expected it to flop before release. It went on to become, adjusted for inflation, one of the highest-grossing films in history and revived the entire science-fiction genre.

examples.hanzi: 这部电视剧下周在北京开拍。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànshìjù xiàzhōu zài Běijīng kāipāi.
examples.english: This TV series starts shooting in Beijing next week.

examples.hanzi: 拍卖会准时开拍,大家请就座。
examples.pinyin: Pāimàihuì zhǔnshí kāipāi, dàjiā qǐng jiùzuò.
examples.english: The auction starts on time, so please take your seats.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a burial in the ground; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
莫 (mò) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 幕 mù, 慕 mù and 募 mù.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.

example.hanzi: 他们每年清明节都会去墓地扫墓。
example.pinyin: Tāmen měinián Qīngmíngjié dōuhuì qù mùdì sǎomù.
example.english: Every year at Qingming Festival, they go to the cemetery to tend the graves.
example.fact: Père Lachaise Cemetery in Paris, opened in 1804, was designed as a landscaped garden cemetery specifically to make burial more appealing after the closure of overcrowded inner-city graveyards. It now holds the remains of figures such as Chopin, Oscar Wilde, and Jim Morrison, drawing millions of visitors annually.

examples.hanzi: 墓地在山坡上,风景很安静。
examples.pinyin: Mùdì zài shānpō shàng, fēngjǐng hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: The cemetery is on the hillside, and the scenery is peaceful.

examples.hanzi: 清明节那天,我们去墓地看望奶奶。
examples.pinyin: Qīngmíng jié nà tiān, wǒmen qù mùdì kànwàng nǎinai.
examples.english: On Qingming Festival, we visit Grandma at the cemetery.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — weather, as in 雪 snow, 雷 thunder, 零 zero. Oldest form: a person waiting out rain; waiting turned into "need".
而 (ér) is only a loose sound hint here; 需 also sounds out 须 xū.
求 (seek) — the original picture of a fur coat (裘 qiú adds 衣); "seek, request" is a borrowed use. 求 sounds out 球 qiú and 救 jiù.

example.hanzi: 市场对新能源汽车的需求正在增长。
example.pinyin: Shìchǎng duì xīn néngyuán qìchē de xūqiú zhèngzài zēngzhǎng.
example.english: Market demand for new-energy vehicles is growing.
example.fact: Norway generates over 90% of its electricity from hydropower, and partly as a result, it has one of the highest rates of electric vehicle adoption in the world. By the early 2020s, battery-electric cars accounted for the large majority of new car sales in the country.

examples.hanzi: 夏天来了,冷饮的需求一下子变多了。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān lái le, lěngyǐn de xūqiú yíxiàzi biàn duō le.
examples.english: Summer has come, and demand for cold drinks has suddenly risen.

examples.hanzi: 我们要先了解客户的需求,再做方案。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào xiān liǎojiě kèhù de xūqiú, zài zuò fāng'àn.
examples.english: We need to understand the customer's needs before making a plan.

meanings: to go up by one grade

components.note: 十 (ten/cross) — the visible part; 升 once was a ladle measuring grain, then 'to rise'. The shape does not explain this. Memory aid: a ladle lifted high.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 给; 级 first meant the order of threads, then rank.
及 (jí) sounds exactly like 级; also 极 jí, 吸 xī.

example.hanzi: 我把手机系统升级到了最新版本。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ shǒujī xìtǒng shēngjí dàole zuìxīn bǎnběn.
example.english: I upgraded my phone's system to the latest version.
example.fact: Moore's Law, an observation made by Intel co-founder Gordon Moore in 1965, predicted that the number of transistors on a computer chip would roughly double every two years. The semiconductor industry sustained something close to that pace for decades, though the rate of improvement has notably slowed since the 2010s.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏升级以后更好玩了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì shēngjí yǐhòu gèng hǎowán le.
examples.english: This game is more fun after the upgrade.

examples.hanzi: 他的小孩今年升级,上三年级了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xiǎohái jīnnián shēngjí, shàng sān niánjí le.
examples.english: His kid moved up a grade this year and is now in third grade.

components.note: 王 (jade, 斜玉旁) — precious jade, an omen of luck; also in 球 ball, 珠 pearl.
耑 (duān) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 端 duān.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 瑞士以精密的钟表制造业闻名。
example.pinyin: Ruìshì yǐ jīngmì de zhōngbiǎo zhìzào yè wénmíng.
example.english: Switzerland is famous for its precision watchmaking industry.
example.fact: Switzerland has remained officially neutral in international conflicts since 1815, following the Congress of Vienna. This long-standing neutrality is part of why Geneva became the historic headquarters of the International Red Cross and, later, several United Nations agencies.

examples.hanzi: 我想去瑞士滑雪,听说那里的雪景很美。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù Ruìshì huáxuě, tīngshuō nàlǐ de xuějǐng hěn měi.
examples.english: I want to go skiing in Switzerland; I hear the snow scenery is beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 瑞士的巧克力很有名。
examples.pinyin: Ruìshì de qiǎokèlì hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: Swiss chocolate is very famous.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pounding and poking by hand; also in 打 hit, 拍 pat.
岛 (dǎo) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 导 dǎo.
舌 (tongue) — the left part, as in 话 speech. Memory aid: too many wagging tongues create chaos, hence 混乱.
乚 (hook) — the right-hand stroke and dictionary radical. 乱 is simplified from 亂; the stroke does not add meaning.

example.hanzi: 那个孩子总是在课堂上捣乱。
example.pinyin: Nàge háizi zǒngshì zài kètáng shàng dǎoluàn.
example.english: That kid is always causing trouble in class.
example.fact: Common ravens are known among corvid researchers for actively provoking other animals, including wolves and foxes, by pulling their tails or stealing food. Scientists believe this teasing behavior helps ravens test which animals might be safe to scavenge from later.

examples.hanzi: 别在这里捣乱,快回你的座位去。
examples.pinyin: Bié zài zhèlǐ dǎoluàn, kuài huí nǐ de zuòwèi qù.
examples.english: Don't cause trouble here; get back to your seat.

examples.hanzi: 小猫跳上桌子捣乱,打翻了杯子。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo māo tiàoshàng zhuōzi dǎoluàn, dǎfānle bēizi.
examples.english: The kitten jumped on the table making mischief and knocked over the cup.

components.note: 纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — twisted threads, a tangle; also in 红 red, 级 level.
丩 (jiū, two strands twisted) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 叫 jiào and 收 shōu.
纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — wrapping with thread; also in 红 red, 级 level.

example.hanzi: 这两件事纠缠在一起,很难分清。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn shì jiūchán zài yīqǐ, hěn nán fēnqīng.
example.english: These two matters are tangled together, hard to distinguish.
example.fact: In physics, quantum entanglement links two particles so that measuring one instantly correlates with the state of the other, no matter the distance between them. Einstein famously distrusted the idea, calling it 'spooky action at a distance,' though decades of experiments, including the 2022 Nobel Prize-winning work of Aspect, Clauser, and Zeilinger, have confirmed the effect is real.

examples.hanzi: 他纠缠了我一个下午,要我借给他钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiūchánle wǒ yí gè xiàwǔ, yào wǒ jiègěi tā qián.
examples.english: He pestered me all afternoon to lend him money.

examples.hanzi: 线团纠缠在一起,怎么也解不开。
examples.pinyin: Xiàntuán jiūchán zài yìqǐ, zěnme yě jiě bù kāi.
examples.english: The balls of thread are tangled together and can't be undone.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — weather radical, as in 雪 snow, 雾 fog; 雷 also sounds out 镭 léi and 蕾 lěi.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 达 is to get through to, to reach.
大 (dà) is only a loose stand-in for the old sound part, so treat it as a rough clue for dá.

example.hanzi: 机场雷达系统全天候监控飞机的位置。
example.pinyin: Jīchǎng léidá xìtǒng quán tiānhòu jiānkòng fēijī de wèizhì.
example.english: The airport's radar system monitors aircraft positions around the clock.
example.fact: Radar technology was developed independently by several nations in the 1930s, but it was Britain's Chain Home radar network, operational just before World War II, that gave the Royal Air Force crucial early warning during the Battle of Britain in 1940. This helped fighter squadrons intercept incoming German aircraft in time.

examples.hanzi: 气象雷达显示明天会有大雨。
examples.pinyin: Qìxiàng léidá xiǎnshì míngtiān huì yǒu dàyǔ.
examples.english: The weather radar shows heavy rain tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 警察用雷达测量车的速度。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá yòng léidá cèliáng chē de sùdù.
examples.english: The police measure a car's speed with radar.

components.note: 寸 (inch; hand) — the lower part, also in 对 and 导. 寿 comes from 壽, an old form of 老 (old) with a sound part; it means long life.
丰 (abundant) — the upper part. Memory aid: abundant years under a careful hand. Sound clue: 寿 appears in 涛 tāo and 筹 chóu loosely.

example.hanzi: 祝您生日快乐，健康长寿！
example.pinyin: Zhù nín shēngrì kuàilè, jiànkāng chángshòu!
example.english: Happy birthday, and wishing you good health and a long life!
example.fact: 寿 is central to birthday culture for the elderly: 寿桃 (longevity peach buns), 寿面 (long noodles) and 做寿 (hold a birthday banquet). It also appears in 寿命 (lifespan) and, borrowed from Japanese, 寿司 (sushi).

examples.hanzi: 奶奶今年八十岁大寿。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai jīnnián bāshí suì dàshòu.
examples.english: Grandma celebrates her eightieth birthday this year.

examples.hanzi: 我们给爷爷买了寿面。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gěi yéye mǎi le shòumiàn.
examples.english: We bought longevity noodles for Grandpa.

components.note: 足 (foot, ⻊) — knees and feet, as in 跑 run, 跳 jump.
危 (wēi) gives a close sound; 诡 guǐ shares it.

example.hanzi: 他跪在地上求她原谅。
example.pinyin: Tā guì zài dì shang qiú tā yuánliàng.
example.english: He knelt on the ground, begging her forgiveness.
example.fact: 跪 is used in 下跪 (to kneel down), 跪拜 (to bow on one's knees) and 磕头 scenes in historical dramas. In modern slang, 跪了 means 'I'm done for / I give up', as if collapsing on one's knees.

examples.hanzi: 孩子跪在地上捡玩具。
examples.pinyin: Háizi guì zài dìshàng jiǎn wánjù.
examples.english: The child is kneeling on the floor picking up toys.

examples.hanzi: 他双膝跪地，向她求婚。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuāng xī guì dì, xiàng tā qiúhūn.
examples.english: He knelt on both knees and proposed to her.

components.note: 灬 (fire, 四点底) — flames below, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 煮 cook.
前 (qián) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 剪 jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 我早上煎了两个蛋。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshang jiān le liǎng gè dàn.
example.english: This morning I fried two eggs.
example.fact: 煎 means pan-frying in a thin layer of oil, unlike 炸 (deep-frying) and 炒 (stir-frying). Pot-stickers and eggs are 煎ed. It also means to simmer herbal medicine: 煎药.

examples.hanzi: 我想煎一条鱼当晚饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng jiān yì tiáo yú dāng wǎnfàn.
examples.english: I want to pan-fry a fish for dinner.

examples.hanzi: 这个煎饼又香又脆。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiānbǐng yòu xiāng yòu cuì.
examples.english: This crepe is fragrant and crispy.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks ground and soil, as in 地, 城, 墙; 堪 is to bear or withstand.
甚 (shèn) is a loose hint for kān; 勘 kān shares it.

example.hanzi: 他累得疲惫不堪。
example.pinyin: Tā lèi de píbèi bùkān.
example.english: He is utterly exhausted.
example.fact: 堪 is literary. The pattern 不堪 means 'unbearably…', as in 疲惫不堪 (exhausted) or 不堪入耳 (unbearable to hear). 堪称 means 'can be called', as in 堪称完美 (can be called perfect).

examples.hanzi: 这个房间脏得不堪入目。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān zāng de bùkān rùmù.
examples.english: This room is so dirty it is unpleasant to look at.

examples.hanzi: 他的处境十分狼狈不堪。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chǔjìng shífēn lángbèi bùkān.
examples.english: His situation is utterly wretched.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 哄 is coaxing, or a din of voices, as in 哄堂大笑.
共 (gòng) — loose sound hint (hōng vs gòng); same part in 洪 hóng.

example.hanzi: 妈妈在哄宝宝睡觉。
example.pinyin: Māma zài hǒng bǎobao shuìjiào.
example.english: Mum is soothing the baby to sleep.
example.fact: 哄 has three readings: hǒng (coax or fool, as in 哄孩子, 哄女朋友 'sweet-talk your girlfriend'), hōng (a roar of laughter, 哄堂大笑) and hòng (uproar, 起哄 'to heckle').

examples.hanzi: 你去哄哄孩子，他在哭。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ qù hǒnghong háizi, tā zài kū.
examples.english: Go and soothe the child, who is crying.

examples.hanzi: 他买了花来哄女朋友开心。
examples.pinyin: Tā mǎi le huā lái hǒng nǚpéngyou kāixīn.
examples.english: He bought flowers to cheer up his girlfriend.

meanings: to set one's mind at rest
to keep one's mind on sth

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 知道飞机安全降落，她终于安心了。
example.pinyin: Zhīdào fēijī ānquán jiàngluò, tā zhōngyú ānxīn le.
example.english: Knowing the plane had landed safely, she finally felt relieved.
example.fact: Commercial aviation is statistically one of the safest ways to travel: the global fatal-accident rate has fallen to a few per ten million flights, thanks largely to redundant systems, collision-avoidance technology, and rigorous crew training. Modern jetliners are also engineered to glide safely for many kilometers even after a complete loss of engine power, giving pilots time to reach a runway.

examples.hanzi: 你放心去吧,家里的事我会处理好,你安心工作。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ fàngxīn qù ba, jiālǐ de shì wǒ huì chǔlǐ hǎo, nǐ ānxīn gōngzuò.
examples.english: Don't worry, go ahead; I'll take care of things at home, so you can work with peace of mind.

examples.hanzi: 吃了药以后,他才能安心睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Chīle yào yǐhòu, tā cái néng ānxīn shuìjiào.
examples.english: Only after taking the medicine could he sleep peacefully.

components.note: 氵 (water) — immersed in water; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
奄 (yǎn) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 掩 yǎn and 腌 yān.
歹 (bad bone) — death and decay, as in 残 remnant, 烈 fierce, 殊 special.
匕 (person) — a person beside bones: death.

example.hanzi: 那个男孩差点在河里淹死。
example.pinyin: Nàge nánhái chàdiǎn zài hé lǐ yānsǐ.
example.english: That boy nearly drowned in the river.
example.fact: The mammalian dive reflex slows a person's heart rate and redirects blood toward vital organs the moment the face is submerged in cold water, a response that is strongest in infants. It is one reason some cold-water drowning victims, especially children, have been successfully resuscitated after unusually long periods underwater.

examples.hanzi: 下雨时,有人在这条河里被淹死了,我们要注意安全。
examples.pinyin: Xiàyǔ shí, yǒu rén zài zhè tiáo hé lǐ bèi yānsǐ le, wǒmen yào zhùyì ānquán.
examples.english: Someone drowned in this river during the rain, so we must be careful.

examples.hanzi: 小心点,别让花被你浇水淹死了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn diǎn, bié ràng huā bèi nǐ jiāoshuǐ yānsǐ le.
examples.english: Careful, don't drown the flowers by overwatering them.

meanings: benefit (provided by an employer or organization)

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and blessings: 神, 礼, 祝, 祈; 福 is good fortune from the gods.
畐 (fú) sounds exactly like 福; also in 幅 fú, 副 fù, 富 fù.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.

example.hanzi: 这家公司为员工提供很好的福利。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī wèi yuángōng tígōng hěn hǎo de fúlì.
example.english: This company provides very good benefits for its employees.
example.fact: Germany introduced the world's first modern social-insurance system in the 1880s under Chancellor Otto von Bismarck, combining sickness, accident, and old-age insurance funded jointly by workers and employers. The model spread across Europe over the following decades and became a template for later national welfare programs, including the U.S. Social Security system created in 1935.

examples.hanzi: 这份工作的福利不错,有五险一金。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn gōngzuò de fúlì búcuò, yǒu wǔxiǎn yì jīn.
examples.english: This job has good benefits, including social insurance and a housing fund.

examples.hanzi: 政府要提高老人的福利。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ yào tígāo lǎorén de fúlì.
examples.english: The government wants to improve welfare for the elderly.

components.note: 贝 (cowrie) — money and value, as in 财, 货, 买: competing for prizes was once tied to offerings and stakes.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 他梦想有一天能拥有一辆赛车。
example.pinyin: Tā mèngxiǎng yǒu yī tiān néng yǒngyǒu yī liàng sàichē.
example.english: He dreams of one day owning a race car.
example.fact: Formula 1 cars generate so much aerodynamic downforce that, in theory, one could drive upside down through a tunnel at racing speed — the airflow beneath and around the car pushes it into the track hard enough to counteract gravity above roughly 130 kilometers per hour.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们去看赛车比赛。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù kàn sàichē bǐsài.
examples.english: This weekend we're going to watch a car race.

examples.hanzi: 他从小就爱玩赛车游戏。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù ài wán sàichē yóuxì.
examples.english: He has loved playing racing games since he was little.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
犭 (animal, dog) — animals, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狂 wild: dogs guard.
讠 (speech) — words and law; 狱 first meant a lawsuit, then a prison.

example.hanzi: 他因表现良好提前出狱了。
example.pinyin: Tā yīn biǎoxiàn liánghǎo tíqián chūyù le.
example.english: He was released from prison early for good behavior.
example.fact: Nelson Mandela was released from South Africa's Victor Verster Prison on 11 February 1990 after 27 years of incarceration, walking free before a global television audience. Four years later he became South Africa's first democratically elected president.

examples.hanzi: 他出狱以后,找了一份新工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā chūyù yǐhòu, zhǎole yí fèn xīn gōngzuò.
examples.english: After being released from prison, he found a new job.

examples.hanzi: 妻子一直在等他出狱,重新开始生活。
examples.pinyin: Qīzi yìzhí zài děng tā chūyù, chóngxīn kāishǐ shēnghuó.
examples.english: His wife has been waiting for him to be released so they can start life over.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
玉 (jade) — jade kept under a roof: treasure. The traditional 寶 also had 贝 (cowrie, money).
艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 is grass and plants, as in 花, 草, 菜; hiding under vegetation — 藏 is to conceal or store.
臧 (zāng) — near sound — 藏 is cáng; 臧 also sounds out 脏 zāng.

example.hanzi: 探险队在山洞深处发现了一批宝藏。
example.pinyin: Tànxiǎnduì zài shāndòng shēnchù fāxiàn le yī pī bǎozàng.
example.english: The expedition team discovered a trove of treasure deep inside the cave.
example.fact: In 2009 a metal detectorist in a Staffordshire farm field unearthed the largest hoard of Anglo-Saxon gold ever found — more than 3,500 items, mostly war gear, dating to around the 7th century AD. The Staffordshire Hoard is now valued at over three million pounds and displayed in museums in Birmingham and Stoke-on-Trent.

examples.hanzi: 这座古城里藏着很多宝藏。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔchéng lǐ cángzhe hěn duō bǎozàng.
examples.english: Many treasures are hidden in this ancient city.

examples.hanzi: 对我来说,图书馆就是一个宝藏。
examples.pinyin: Duì wǒ lái shuō, túshūguǎn jiù shì yí gè bǎozàng.
examples.english: To me, the library is a treasure trove.

components.note: 田 (field) — animals raised on farmland; also in 男 male, 界 border. Read chù for livestock, xù for to raise.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 农场里养着各种畜生，比如牛和羊。
example.pinyin: Nóngchǎng lǐ yǎng zhe gèzhǒng chùsheng, bǐrú niú hé yáng.
example.english: The farm keeps all kinds of livestock, such as cattle and sheep.
example.fact: Cattle were domesticated from wild aurochs roughly 10,500 years ago in the Near East, and genetic studies show nearly all modern cattle breeds descend from a surprisingly small founding population of around 80 female aurochs. The aurochs itself survived in the wild until 1627, when the last known individual died in Poland's Jaktorów Forest.

examples.hanzi: 农民把畜生都赶回了圈里。
examples.pinyin: Nóngmín bǎ chùshēng dōu gǎnhuíle quān lǐ.
examples.english: The farmer drove all the livestock back into the pen.

examples.hanzi: 古时候,人们靠畜生耕地。
examples.pinyin: Gǔ shíhou, rénmen kào chùshēng gēngdì.
examples.english: In ancient times, people relied on farm animals to plow the land.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and flowers, as in 草, 茶, 菜; 花 is a flower.
化 (huà) hints at the sound: 花 huā is close, and 化 also gives 华 huá and 货 huò.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — money and trade: 财, 货, 买, 贵; 费 is a cost or fee.
弗 (fú) is close to fèi; same part in 沸 fèi.

example.hanzi: 装修这套房子花费了他们大量的时间和金钱。
example.pinyin: Zhuāngxiū zhè tào fángzi huāfèi le tāmen dàliàng de shíjiān hé jīnqián.
example.english: Renovating this apartment cost them a great deal of time and money.
example.fact: The Sydney Opera House was originally budgeted at about 7 million Australian dollars and estimated to take four years to build; it ended up costing roughly 102 million dollars and took fourteen years, opening in 1973. Its architect, Jørn Utzon, resigned from the project in 1966 and never saw the finished building in person.

examples.hanzi: 这次旅行花费了我们不少钱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng huāfèile wǒmen bù shǎo qián.
examples.english: This trip cost us quite a lot of money.

examples.hanzi: 我不想花费太多时间在路上。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng huāfèi tài duō shíjiān zài lùshang.
examples.english: I don't want to spend too much time on the road.

components.note: 犭 (animal, 反犬旁) — beasts and hunting dogs, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf.

example.hanzi: 他以打猎为生。
example.pinyin: Tā yǐ dǎliè wéi shēng.
example.english: He makes a living by hunting.
example.fact: 猎 shows up in 打猎 (to hunt), 猎人 (hunter), 猎物 (prey) and 猎奇 (to seek novelty). 猎头 is the modern term for a headhunter, a recruiter.

examples.hanzi: 猎人带着狗上山了。
examples.pinyin: Lièrén dài zhe gǒu shàng shān le.
examples.english: The hunter went up the mountain with his dog.

examples.hanzi: 这只狐狸正在捕猎兔子。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī húli zhèngzài bǔliè tùzi.
examples.english: This fox is hunting rabbits.

components.note: 珏 (two jades) — the same strings shape as in 琴 qín; 瑟 is a large zither, seen in 琴瑟 and foreign names.

example.hanzi: 他冷得瑟瑟发抖。
example.pinyin: Tā lěng de sèsè fādǒu.
example.english: He was shivering with cold.
example.fact: In 瑟瑟 the word describes a rustling or trembling, as in 秋风瑟瑟 or 瑟瑟发抖. By itself 瑟 is an ancient 25-string zither; the famous pairing 琴瑟 is a poetic symbol of a harmonious marriage.

examples.hanzi: 寒风吹过，树叶瑟瑟作响。
examples.pinyin: Hánfēng chuī guò, shùyè sèsè zuòxiǎng.
examples.english: As the cold wind blows past, the leaves rustle.

examples.hanzi: 他害怕得瑟瑟发抖。
examples.pinyin: Tā hàipà de sèsè fādǒu.
examples.english: He trembled with fear.

components.note: 甘 (sweet) — a mouth 口 holding something 一 in it: a sweet taste, as in 甘甜, then willing, as in 甘愿.

example.hanzi: 他甘愿为你付出。
example.pinyin: Tā gānyuàn wèi nǐ fùchū.
example.english: He is willing to give for you.
example.fact: 甘 is a literary word for sweet and for willingness: 甘心 (resigned willingly), 甘甜 (sweet), 同甘共苦 (share joys and hardships). Gān is also a short name for Gansu province (甘肃).

examples.hanzi: 我们愿意甘苦与共。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yuànyì gānkǔ yǔ gòng.
examples.english: We are willing to share joys and hardships together.

examples.hanzi: 她不甘心就这样放弃。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù gānxīn jiù zhèyàng fàngqì.
examples.english: She is not willing to give up just like that.

components.note: 上 (above) — 上 over 下 squeezed together: something stuck in the middle, the sense of qiǎ (to wedge); kǎ is the borrowed sound for "card" and "car", as in 信用卡 and 卡车.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 卡特总统在任期内积极推动人权外交。
example.pinyin: Kǎtè zǒngtǒng zài rènqī nèi jījí tuīdòng rénquán wàijiāo.
example.english: President Carter actively promoted human-rights diplomacy during his term.
example.fact: Jimmy Carter, the 39th U.S. president, lived to 100 years old, longer than any other former U.S. president in history, and died in December 2024. After leaving office in 1981 he spent decades building homes with Habitat for Humanity and helped negotiate the 1978 Camp David Accords, for which he later received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2002.

examples.hanzi: 卡特先生是我们的新邻居。
examples.pinyin: Kǎtè xiānsheng shì wǒmen de xīn línjū.
examples.english: Mr. Carter is our new neighbor.

examples.hanzi: 我的同事卡特每天骑车上班。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tóngshì Kǎtè měitiān qí chē shàngbān.
examples.english: My colleague Carter cycles to work every day.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
马 (horse) — marks horses and riding, as in 骑 ride, 骂 scold, 驾 drive; 骚 is to stir up or annoy, as in 骚扰.
蚤 (zǎo, flea) hints at the sound: 骚 sāo is close to 搔 sāo (scratch).
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 扰 is to stir up and disturb.
尤 (yóu) is only a loose sound hint for rǎo.

example.hanzi: 公司专门设立了举报性骚扰的渠道。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī zhuānmén shèlì le jǔbào xìng sāorǎo de qúdào.
example.english: The company set up a dedicated channel for reporting sexual harassment.
example.fact: The term "sexual harassment" was popularized in the United States in the mid-1970s by a group of women at Cornell University, and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission did not formally recognize it as a form of illegal sex discrimination until 1980. The phrase "Me Too" itself was coined by activist Tarana Burke in 2006, more than a decade before it went viral globally in 2017.

examples.hanzi: 公司要求所有员工参加预防性骚扰的培训。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī yāoqiú suǒyǒu yuángōng cānjiā yùfáng xìng sāorǎo de péixùn.
examples.english: The company requires all employees to attend training on preventing sexual harassment.

examples.hanzi: 性骚扰是违法的,受害者可以报警。
examples.pinyin: Xìng sāorǎo shì wéifǎ de, shòuhàizhě kěyǐ bàojǐng.
examples.english: Sexual harassment is illegal, and victims can call the police.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — leading an ox by a rope; as a part, 牛 marks cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 特 special, 牧 herd.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 扯 is to tear or pull.
止 (zhǐ) is a loose hint for chě.

example.hanzi: 这起案件牵扯到好几家公司。
example.pinyin: Zhè qǐ ànjiàn qiānchě dào hǎo jǐ jiā gōngsī.
example.english: This case involves several companies.
example.fact: The 2015 Volkswagen "Dieselgate" emissions scandal eventually implicated multiple automakers across the industry after investigators found software designed to cheat pollution tests. Volkswagen alone has paid more than 30 billion euros in fines, buybacks, and settlements worldwide since the scandal broke.

examples.hanzi: 这件事牵扯到很多人,不好处理。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì qiānchě dào hěn duō rén, bù hǎo chǔlǐ.
examples.english: This matter involves many people and is hard to handle.

examples.hanzi: 我不想被牵扯进他们的家庭矛盾。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng bèi qiānchě jìn tāmen de jiātíng máodùn.
examples.english: I don't want to get dragged into their family conflict.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — birds, here the eagle; also in 难, 谁, 集.
周 (zhōu) is a loose clue; 调 diào and 凋 diāo share it and sound the same as 雕.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 像 is a person's likeness.
象 (xiàng, elephant) gives the exact sound; 象 first meant elephant, then "image".

example.hanzi: 广场中央立着一座巨大的雕像。
example.pinyin: Guǎngchǎng zhōngyāng lì zhe yī zuò jùdà de diāoxiàng.
example.english: A huge statue stands in the middle of the square.
example.fact: Michelangelo's marble statue of David, completed in 1504, stands over 5.17 meters tall and was carved from a single block of Carrara marble that two earlier sculptors had already abandoned as flawed decades before. Its head and hands are deliberately oversized relative to its body, a technique thought to compensate for the original plan to display it high on a cathedral roofline it never reached.

examples.hanzi: 博物馆里有一座古希腊的雕像。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn lǐ yǒu yí zuò gǔ Xīlà de diāoxiàng.
examples.english: The museum has an ancient Greek statue.

examples.hanzi: 这座雕像是用石头刻成的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò diāoxiàng shì yòng shítou kè chéng de.
examples.english: This statue was carved from stone.

meanings: start explaining and it's a long story
complicated and not easy to express succinctly

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.hanzi: 我们怎么认识的？说来话长。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zěnme rènshi de? Shuōláihuàcháng.
example.english: How did we meet? It's a long story.
example.fact: The Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic poem, is roughly ten times the combined length of Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, running to about 200,000 verse lines — making it one of the longest single literary works ever composed within a single tradition.

examples.hanzi: 我为什么会来中国?说来话长。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wèishénme huì lái Zhōngguó? Shuōlái huà cháng.
examples.english: Why did I come to China? It's a long story.

examples.hanzi: 这件事说来话长,等吃完饭我再告诉你。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì shuōlái huà cháng, děng chīwán fàn wǒ zài gàosu nǐ.
examples.english: It's a long story; I'll tell you after dinner.
